body:
Most US background checks take 1 to 5 business days. Slower checks (FBI fingerprint, international records, courts on holiday) can stretch to 30 days or more. The exact wait depends on the check types you order, where the data lives, and how complete the candidate's information is on day one.

The table below shows typical turnaround by check type. The rest of this guide walks through each one, the most common reasons checks stall, and what you can do as an employer to speed yours up.

Background check turnaround at a glance

Check typeTypical turnaroundSlowest case
SSN / identity verificationUnder 1 day2 to 3 days if data is mismatched
Criminal records (instant database)Under 1 hourSame-day
Criminal records (county courthouse)1 to 7 business days14+ days if the court is closed
Criminal records (FBI fingerprint)3 to 7 business days (LiveScan)8 to 12 weeks if mailed
MVR (driving record)Real-time in most states1 to 3 days in CA, NY
Employment verification3 to 5 business days2 weeks if employer is unresponsive
Education verification3 to 7 business days4 weeks for international schools
Credit checkInstant3 to 5 days if the file is frozen
Drug test (5-panel urine)1 to 3 business days1 week if lab confirmation is needed
Professional license verification1 to 3 days1 week if the board verifies manually
International background check2 to 4 weeks8+ weeks for some countries

What is a background check?

A background check is a structured review of a candidate's history before hire. Employers run them to verify the resume, screen for risk, and meet regulatory requirements in industries like healthcare, transportation, finance, and childcare.

A typical pre-employment screen bundles several individual checks: identity verification, criminal record search, MVR, employment and education verification, sometimes a credit pull or drug test. Each component runs on its own timeline because each one pulls from a different source. The total wait is set by your slowest component, not your fastest.

How long does an employment background check take?

A standard pre-employment background check takes 3 to 5 business days end to end.

That timeline assumes three things:

  • The candidate signs the consent and disclosure form on day one
  • Your screening provider runs all components in parallel (most do, but ask)
  • No single component stalls (the bottleneck sets the total)

According to Goodhire's benchmark data, about 80% of standard checks return within five business days, and roughly half close in under three.

The biggest single thing employers control: the consent form. A complete, FCRA-compliant background check form captures the candidate's full legal name, date of birth, SSN, seven-year address history, and signed authorization in one go. Missing data is the single most common reason a check stalls on day one.

How long does a criminal background check take?

A criminal background check has the widest range of any single component.

Instant database search: Under 1 hour. Most providers run a multi-state criminal database search first to flag potential matches.

County courthouse search: 1 to 7 business days. The provider sends a researcher (or runs a county database query) to verify any hits or pull records the instant database missed. Court closures, holidays, and short-staffed clerks all stretch this.

State repository search: 1 to 3 business days when the state has an API connection (CA, NY, FL, TX, IL, GA). Up to 14 business days for smaller states that handle requests manually.

FBI fingerprint check (LiveScan or FD-258 card): 3 to 7 business days for digital LiveScan submissions. 8 to 12 weeks if the prints are mailed to the FBI's Criminal Justice Information Services Division. The FBI documents the current processing times on its identity history page.

The wide range exists because the United States has no single criminal database. Records are split across more than 3,000 county courthouses, 50 state repositories, the FBI's NCIC, and federal court records (PACER). A thorough check touches several of those in sequence.

How long does an MVR (driving record) check take?

For most states, an MVR returns in real time, often within 5 minutes, through an API connection to the state DMV. The exceptions:

  • California, New York: 1 to 3 business days
  • A handful of smaller states: same day, but only during business hours

If the role doesn't involve driving, skip the MVR. It saves time and money.

How long does employment verification take?

Employment verification runs 3 to 5 business days on average. The variable is the previous employer:

  • Large companies that use The Work Number (Equifax): instant to 1 day
  • Mid-size companies with an HR contact: 1 to 3 business days
  • Small businesses with no formal HR: 5 to 10 business days
  • Companies that have closed, merged, or gone bankrupt: 2+ weeks or alternative documentation (W-2, paystubs)

The candidate can help. Ask them to list a direct supervisor and an HR contact on the application, not just the company name. Pair the application with a structured reference check form template so references are captured before the offer goes out.

How long does education verification take?

Education verification runs 3 to 7 business days for US institutions.

Faster cases: the school is on the National Student Clearinghouse network, which covers most US colleges and universities. Results return same-day to next-day.

Slower cases:

  • High schools (not on the Clearinghouse, manual registrar verification)
  • Schools that have closed
  • International degrees (2 to 4 weeks, may require a credential evaluation)

If the role doesn't require the specific degree, consider whether you need the check at all. Each verification adds 3+ days to the total wait.

How long does a state background check take?

State checks fall into two buckets.

API-connected states (CA, FL, NY, TX, IL, GA, and others): 1 to 3 business days. Some return same-day for in-state criminal records.

Manual states: 5 to 14 business days. The provider mails or faxes a request to the state repository and waits.

A few states (DE, ME, NH) restrict what employers can pull at the state level. Your provider will route those to the county level instead, which slows the timeline.

How long does an international background check take?

International checks take 2 to 4 weeks minimum. Some countries take 8+ weeks. Records often have to be requested in person, by mail, or through a local agent, and document translation adds time on top.

If you are hiring international remote employees, build the international check into your offer timeline early. Treat the formal start date as the date the check clears, not the date the offer is signed.

What causes delays in the background check process?

The most common causes, in order of how often we see each one:

  1. Incomplete consent form. Missing date of birth, partial address history, no SSN. Triggers a back-and-forth with the candidate that costs a full day or more.
  2. Common name. "John Smith" pulls dozens of potential matches across counties. The provider has to disambiguate by date of birth and address.
  3. Court closures. US courts close for federal holidays, county-specific holidays, and inclement weather. Some county courts also run a 4-day week.
  4. Frozen credit report. The candidate's credit file is frozen with one of the bureaus. The candidate has to lift the freeze, which adds 2 to 3 days.
  5. Unresponsive past employer. The HR contact does not return calls or emails. The provider typically follows up 3 times before escalating.
  6. International components. Records have to be requested by mail in some countries. Document translation and credential evaluation add time.
  7. FCRA dispute. The candidate disputes a finding on the report. The investigation has up to 30 days under the FCRA.

The first three account for most delays. The first one is the only one fully within your control.

How to speed up your background check process

Seven tactics that move the needle, in order of impact:

  1. Use a structured, FCRA-compliant consent form. Capture full legal name, date of birth, SSN, and seven-year address history at intake. Pre-built compliant templates do this for you (and the disclosure and authorization language is already wired in).
  2. Collect reference contacts on the application, not after the offer. Direct supervisor name, title, current contact info. Do not accept "HR" as a contact.
  3. Pre-validate SSN format on the form. Saves a 24-hour back-and-forth when the candidate transposed two digits.
  4. Use a screening provider with API-based criminal and MVR lookups. Real-time hits return in minutes instead of days.
  5. Communicate the timeline to the candidate upfront. "Expect 3 to 5 business days. We will email you on day 5 if it is still in progress." Cuts down on candidate anxiety and reduces dropouts.
  6. Use a contingent offer letter. The candidate signs, accepts, and gives notice while the check is running. You preserve your offer window.
  7. Tie the check to the application form. When the job application form template and consent form share the same fields, you skip re-entry on day one.

The takeaway

Most checks land in 3 to 5 business days. The fastest path runs through a complete consent form, an API-connected screening provider, and a candidate who knows what to expect. The slowest checks happen when missing information, court closures, or unresponsive past employers stack up.

If you are running checks at any kind of volume, the single biggest lever is the form itself. A complete, FCRA-compliant, signed-on-day-one consent flow eliminates the most common cause of delay before the check even starts.

Background check turnaround FAQ

Why is my background check still pending after 10 days?
Three likely reasons. First, a county courthouse search is in progress and the court is short-staffed or closed. Second, a past employer is not responding to verification requests. Third, the candidate's consent form had incomplete information and the provider is waiting on clarification. Ask your provider which component is the bottleneck, they will usually tell you within a single email.
Can a background check be completed in 1 day?
Yes, for limited checks. An instant database criminal search, SSN trace, and MVR can all complete the same day, often within an hour. A full pre-employment check with employment and education verification cannot be done in one day because those components require human responses from former employers and schools.
What is the average background check turnaround time?
For a standard US pre-employment screen (identity + criminal + MVR + employment + education), the average is 3 to 5 business days. Add a credit check or drug test and add 1 to 2 days. Add international records and the average jumps to 2 to 4 weeks.
Can I move forward with the hire before the background check clears?
You can extend a contingent offer. The candidate signs and accepts contingent on a clean check. You preserve your offer window without skipping the screen. Do not put the candidate on payroll before the check clears in regulated industries (healthcare, transportation, finance, childcare).
Do background checks expire?
Yes. Most employers re-run a check if the existing one is more than 30 days old, and a fresh check is required if more than 6 months have passed. Some industries (DOT, healthcare) require annual re-checks.
Can I see my own background check?
Yes. Under the FCRA, candidates have the right to see the full report and dispute anything inaccurate. If you are an employer, you must give the candidate a copy of the report before taking adverse action based on it.
